full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-5 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 23-9-2020 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Cox's Bazar in Samabay Miscellaneous Case No. 28 of 2013 allowing the appeal and setting-aside the judgment and order dated 14-2-2013 passed by the Deputy Registrar (Judicial), Divisional Co-operative Directorate, Chattogram in Appeal Case No. 34 of 2013 affirming the judgment and order dated 23-10-2012 passed by the District Co-operative Officer, Cox's Bazar in Dispute Case No. 23 of 2012 affirming the judgment and order dated 8-3-2012 passed by Arbitration Committee of Badarkhali Samabay Krishi-o-Upanibesh Samity in Arbitration Case No. 36 of 2012 should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Material facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, briefly, are that the opposite parties as applicants (herein after called as "the opposite party") filed Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 36 of 2012 challenging the deed of transfer made by their predecessor Hafeza Khatun contending, inter-alia that the transfer of the land in question by Hafeza Khatun was illegal because the said Hafeza Khatun was not a member of the Samity and as per provision of by-law 8(Cha) of the said Samity, no prior approval of transfer has been taken in respect of transfer of the land in question. 

 3. The present petitioner, Muhammad Abdur Rashid and opposite party Nos. 6-7 contested the case by filing written objection denying all the material allegations made in the application stating, inter-alia, that the land in question was duly transferred according to agreement dated 20-7-2007, it is on record that an application for transfer was made by the member, Abdur Rashid, husband of Hafeza Khatun as per provision of by-law 8(Cha) of the Samity and pursuant to the said application on 5-11-2007 Taka 10,000 was deposited to the Samity as per provisions of 8(ja) of by-law and thereafter,- on 12-11-2007 the balance amount was paid to Hafeza Khatun and accordingly she executed a sale deed in favour of ATM Jahangir Alam (herein opposite party No.6). The approval for transfer was given by the Samity on 7-1-2009 in accordance with law, the applicants filed the case on false allegation and, as such, the case is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. Thereafter, seven members Arbitration Board after hearing the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 36 of 2012 by its judgment and order 8-3-2012 dismissed the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case. Against which the opposite party Nos. 1-5 preferred Dispute Case No. 23 of 2012 before the learned District Samabay Officer, Cox's Bazar, who upon hearing the parties by his judgment and order dated 23-10-2012 dismissed the Dispute Case and affirmed the judgment and order passed by the 7 member Arbitration Board in Arbitration Case No. 36 of 2012. 

 5. Aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and order dated 23-10-2012 passed by the learned District Samabay Officer, Cox's Bazar in Dispute Case No. 23 of 2012, the opposite parties preferred Appeal Case No. 34 of 2012 before the Deputy Registrar (Judicial), Divisional Co-operative Directorate and Appellate Officer, who upon hearing the parties and on considering the materials on record by his judgment and order dated 14-2-2013 dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and order passed in Dispute Case No. 23 of 2012. 

 6. In this backdrop, the present opposite party Nos. 1-5 as applicants filed Samabay Miscellaneous Case No. 28 of 2013 before the learned District Judge, Cox's Bazar as per provision of section 42 of the  সমবায় সমিতি আইন, ২০০১ which was subsequently transmitted to the Court of the learned Additional District Judge, Cox's Bazar for disposal, who after hearing both the parties by the impugned judgment and order dated 23-9-2020 reversed the judgment and order passed by all the forums below. 

 8. Mr Manzur Al Matin, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner in the course of his argument takes me through the judgments of all 3 forums below together with the impugned judgment and then submits that findings of the learned Additional District Judge that Hafeza Khatun, the predecessor of the petitioner without taking prior permission from the Samabay Samity as per law transferred the case land on 12-11-2007 is not correct inasmuch as it is on record that the predecessor of the present petitioner Hafeza Khatun, wife of Abadur Rahman and daughter of Nur Hossain before transferring the case land filed an application before the appropriate authority of the Samabay Board and thereafter, she deposited Taka 10,000 as fees and thereafter, under the full satisfaction of the authority of the Samabay Board she transferred the case land and thereafter, the concerned committee of the Samabay Board by order dated 7-1-2009 approved the transfer. The learned Advocate further submits, it is on record that all the lower forums came to the conclusion that Hafeza Khatun before transferring the case land applied before the authority and deposited sale fees, which was approved by the authority and therefore, Hafeza Khatun, the predecessor of the petitioner justly transferred the case land in accordance with law. Finally, the learned Advocate submits that the present opposite party Nos. 1-5 were well acquainted about the transfer proceedings from the very beginning but the reason best known to them as to why they kept silent over a period of 4 years 6 months and thereafter, the present opposite party Nos. 1-5 filed arbitration case long lapse of more than 4 years 6 months as test case in order to get illegal benefit and all the lower forums considering all these aspects of the case on assigning sound reasons rightly rejected the case by their back to back judgment and order dated 8-3-2012, 23-10-2012 and 14-2-2013 respectively although the learned Additional District Judge without applying his judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case and law bearing on the subject abruptly reversed all the judgments of the lower forums of the Samabay Board on the finding that without prior approval, the predecessor of the petitioner transferred the case land which is contrary to law and, as such, the same is not tenable in law although the provision as to transfer in question without prior approval from the authority is not mandatory which is mere directory and as such, the learned Additional District Judge in setting aside judgments of all 3 lower forums committed an error of law resulting in an error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 10. I have considered the submission of the learned Advocates for both the sides and perused the judgments of all 3 forums below together with the impugned judgment and order dated 23-9-2023 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Cox's Bazar in Samabay Miscellaneous Case No. 28 of 2013 and other materials on record. 

 11. On scrutiny of the record, it appears that on 27-10-2007 Hafeza Khatun, wife of Abdur Rarunan and daughter of Nur Hossain filed an application to the Secretary, Badarkhali Samabay Krishi 0 Upanibesh Samity under the caption: “জমি হস্তান্তরের অনুমতি প্রদানের আবেদন" Thereafter, the said Hafeza Khatun paid fees amounting to Taka 10,000 for transfer of the case to the samity on 5-11-2007 and thereafter, Hafeza Khatun transferred the case land on 12-11-2007. Thereafter, the authority of the Samabay Samity allowed the application under the caption: “জমি হস্তান্তরের অনুমতি প্রদানের আবেদন" on 7-1-2009 without any objection from any quarter. 

 12. On scrutiny of the 3 consecutive judgments passed by various authorities of Samabay Samity, it appears to me that the authorities of the Samabay Samity considered all the relevant documents and thereafter, by their judgments rejected the Arbitration Case. At first, seven members Arbitration Board after hearing the application filed by the present opposite parties as applicants being Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 36 of 2012 challenging the deed of transfer made by Hafeza Khatun by their judgment and order dated 8-3-2012 dismissed the Arbitration Case in the following language— 

 14. Thereafter, in Dispute Case No. 23 of 2012 the Arbitrator and District Samabay Officer observed that— 

 15. This finding of the Arbitrator and District Samabay Officer certainly indicates that the District Samabay Officer considered all the material aspects of the case and thereafter recorded the order of rejection. 

 18. On a close perusal of the record, it appears that the learned Additional District Judge, Cox's Bazar in its turn without applying his judicial mind into the facts of the case and law bearing on the subject abruptly set-aside back to back 3 (three) well founded judgments of the lower forums on the ground that Hafeza Khatun, the predecessor of the petitioner without prior permission of transfer from the Samity as per provision of by-law 8 (Cha) of the Samity transferred the case land, which is illegal and void. 

 19. In the case of Abdur Rahim Afroze vs BC Aga and Co. Ltd. and others reported in 29 DLR (SC) 215 and in the case of Kohinoor Chemical Company Ltd. and others vs Eastern Shippers and Traders Ltd. reported in 41 DLR 387, it has been consistently held that in determining whether a provision of law is mandatory or directory, the intention of the legislature is to be considered by taking account of the entire legislation, and a substantive compliance of the provisions of law should suffice, where no consequence is prescribed. 

 20. In the instant case, in compliance of Rule 8(Chha) of the By-Laws of `Badar Khali Krishi 0 Upanibesh Samiti' the present petitioner applied for prior-approval of the sale in question, and paid the requisite fees within time. Approval was also accorded to the said transfer by the `Samiti'. The mere fact that, the approval was granted after the transfer, cannot vitiate the transfer itself, because the By-Laws do not provide any consequence for obtaining an approval after the transfer takes place. As I have already noticed that in the present case there has been substantive compliance of the provision of law, by applying for prior approval of transfer and subsequent approval thereof, and, as such, the learned Additional District Judge, Cox's Bazar in reversing the decisions of affirmance upholding the transfer, on the mere ground that approval was granted after the transfer took place. 

 23. By the way, it may be observed that the decision reported in 33 DLR (AD) 311 cited by the learned Advocate for the opposite parties has no manner of application in the facts and circumstance of the case inasmuch as the facts of the instant case are quite distinguishable from the facts of the cited case. 

 24. For the reasons stated above the impugned judgment and order dated 23-9-2023 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Cox's Bazar in Samabay Miscellaneous Case No. 28 of 2013 does not deserve to be sustained. 

 25. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and order dated 23-9-2020 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Cox's Bazar in Samabay Miscellaneous Case No. 28 of 2013 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and order dated 14-2-2013 passed by the Deputy Registrar (Judicial), Divisional Co-operative Directorate, Chattogram in Appeal Case No. 34 of 2013 affirming the judgment and order dated 23-10-2012 pas ed by the District Co-operative Officer, Cox's Bazar in Dispute Case No. 23 of 2012 passed by Arbitration Committee of Badarkhali Samabay Krishi 0 Upanibesh Samity in Arbitration Case No. 36 of 2012 is set-aside and consequently, the judgment and order 8-3-2012 passed by Arbitration Committee of Badarkhali Samabay Krishi-o-Upanibesh Samity in Arbitration Case No. 36 of 2012 is restored. The order of status-quo granted earlier by this Court stands vacated.
